solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Britain to consider abolishing right to summon

indicators.note: abolishing says the right is done away with, struck out of the word for consider

parts.note: to reckon is to consider or judge

explanation.surface: A government plan for Britain to look again at doing away with the right to call someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon someone is to signal them to come over, a gestured form of calling for them.

clue.text: Intake of Russians from Baltic regularly identified in uprising

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals, first, third and fifth

parts.note: every other letter of Baltic is taken, starting with the first

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the short word reads from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Something Russians take in from the Baltic is regularly spotted in a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small buckwheat pancakes, a traditional food that Russians eat.

clue.text: Stricture (non-US, surprisingly) applied to American animal

indicators.note: surprisingly says the remaining letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: the fodder whose letters, minus the two named, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strict rule, oddly not for the US, is imposed on an American beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-US' says U and S leave STRICTURE; the letters left over are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Critter is a US dialect variant of creature, used for any living animal.

clue.text: Frenzied dog, having lost head over drink, beginning to champ

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the dog part sits above the drink
having lost head means the dog's first letter is dropped

parts.note: a corgi is a small Welsh breed of dog
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: only the first letter of champ is wanted

explanation.surface: A wild dog gone over the top with drink starts champing.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic describes wild, unrestrained revelry, the frenzy of an orgy.

clue.text: Track time being spent in charge of stage

indicators.note: time being spent means the time is used up and gone, so it drops out of the trail word

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves, which hounds track

explanation.surface: A stage manager running out of time on getting a track ready for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like a verb but is the noun scent, a trail; it loses its T and gains IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic can mean relating to theatrical scenery, the painted sets of a stage production.

clue.text: Weird to disregard UN, but shrewd

indicators.note: to disregard says those two letters are ignored and dropped from the word

parts.note: uncanny means strange or weird
taken as the letters UN

explanation.surface: It's odd to ignore the United Nations, but it can be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means sharp-witted and careful, especially about money or business.

clue.text: Two sorts of drama — one incomplete and a lost cause

indicators.note: one incomplete says the second drama loses its final letter

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama and opera is sung drama

explanation.surface: Two kinds of theatre, one unfinished, and a hopeless case.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, a person or thing written off.

clue.text: 80% of contraband affected by charge imposed on business

indicators.note: affected means those letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: contraband has ten letters, so eighty per cent of it is its first eight
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' as in three by four

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods hit by a levy placed on companies.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTRABA rearranged gives CARBONTA, then X for 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon tax is a levy on fuel emissions, typically placed on companies that burn fossil fuels.

clue.text: News of tense old divisions in Yorkshire originally withheld

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: originally points at the opening letter, and withheld says that first letter is kept back

parts.note: the Ridings were the three historic administrative divisions of Yorkshire, abolished in 1974

explanation.surface: A report of strained relations in Yorkshire's old divisions being kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically split into North, East and West Ridings; drop the opening R of RIDINGS and put T in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news or information received.

clue.text: Contribution from branch or subdivision gives firm security

indicators.note: Contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A company's branch or subdivision chips in to make the firm financially secure.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor holds a ship firmly in place, so to anchor is to make something steady and secure.

clue.text: High flier's very low score on course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large seabird that soars for long distances; the 's stands for is
second meaning: a golf score of three under par on a hole

explanation.walkthrough: The bird reading and the golf reading are two separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The large seabird glides high over oceans, and golfers name a three-under-par hole after it.

clue.text: Competitor takes us in with article in French on Nancy's extreme geographical feature

indicators.note: takes ... in means the competitor word swallows the following piece inside it
in completes the phrase takes us in, putting the paper's initials inside

parts.note: a rival is a competitor
the clue appears in the Financial Times, so 'us' is FT, the paper's own initials
le is a French definite article

indicators.note: extreme means the very end letter of the name it follows

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, fitting the French article; only its last letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A rival talks a French-speaking group in Nancy into something, with an article in the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the newspaper itself: in the Financial Times, 'us' gives FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift valley is a long depression formed where the earth's crust has sunk between faults, such as East Africa's Great Rift.

clue.text: Trick sausage short of ingredients next to its skin

indicators.text: short of ingredients next to its skin
indicators.note: the sausage loses the filling letters sitting just inside its outer letters, the second and the second-to-last

parts.note: a polony is a type of cooked smoked sausage

explanation.surface: A con involving a sausage skimped on the filling just under its casing.
explanation.walkthrough: POLONY's skin is its outer P and Y; the letters next to them, the O after P and the N before Y, are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning manoeuvre or tactic designed to gain an advantage, much like a trick.

clue.text: Rodin's first sculpture about to explode

indicators.note: about means the sculpture goes round the letter

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the sculptor's name

parts.note: Rodin was the French sculptor; his initial letter is wanted

explanation.surface: Rodin's earliest sculpture is on the point of blowing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to break open suddenly and violently, as a balloon does.

clue.text: Blame spy recklessly injecting heroin for profane outburst

indicators.note: injecting means the drug's letter is put inside the rearranged letters
recklessly means the letters are thrown about into a new arrangement

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Accusing a spy rashly of shooting up heroin draws a stream of swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasphemy is irreverent speech about God or sacred things, a profane utterance.

clue.text: Clergyman omitting canticle's conclusion in service is correct

indicators.note: in means the shortened clergyman sits inside the tennis serve

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis

indicators.note: omitting says that final letter of the hymn is left out of the clergyman

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman in a parish

indicators.note: conclusion picks the closing letter of the hymn word

parts.note: a canticle is a hymn sung in church services; only its final letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A curate who leaves out the end of a hymn during a church service is still doing it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a church service, but it is a tennis serve: an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means free from error, exactly right, which is what correct means.

clue.text: Transport route to go round hospital following strike

indicators.note: following says the hospital letter comes after the strike word

parts.note: to cycle is to go round in a repeating circuit
to pat is to strike lightly
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A transport route goes round a hospital after a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle path is a lane set aside for bicycles, a way for travelling by bike.

clue.text: Tips from Pretoria's drivers' club about police vehicle

parts.note: the tips of Pretoria are its first and last letters, P and A, read out as 'P and A'

indicators.note: about says the club's letters are turned round

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Pointers from a South African motoring club concerning a police car.
explanation.walkthrough: The end letters of Pretoria are P and A, and the clue wants that phrase written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A panda car was a British patrol car, so called because of its black-and-white or blue-and-white livery.

clue.text: Raised hat to girl in novel predicament

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word reads upwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel of that name

explanation.surface: A man tips his hat to a fictional heroine and finds himself in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a situation requiring a hard choice between two options, an awkward spot.

clue.text: Manx cat and unnamed cat producing something in the flower bed

indicators.note: a Manx cat famously has no tail, so the word for the animal loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as the plain word for the animal

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so unnamed means N is taken out

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A tailless Manx cat and some nameless moggy messing about in a garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx breed has no tail, so CAT loses its T; LYNX loses N, the abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: The calyx is the ring of sepals around a flower's base, part of the bloom itself in a garden plot.

clue.text: Trouble arising about decoration on floor of industrial plant

indicators.note: about means the upturned trouble word goes round the rest
in a down clue, arising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the decoration sits above the next letter

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: the floor of a word in a down clue is its bottom, its last letter

parts.note: only the last letter of industrial is wanted

explanation.surface: Trouble brewing over a decoration on the shop floor of an industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'industrial plant' reads as a factory, but 'plant' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering garden plant, often grown in hanging baskets for its blue flowers.

clue.text: People outwardly lacking go inwardly gaining a stone

indicators.note: inwardly gaining means the remaining letters take a new letter in their middle
outwardly lacking means the letters removed come from the outside of the word, at its ends

parts.note: taken as the word itself
to go is slang for to urinate, so 'go' gives PEE

explanation.surface: Lifeless people who seem to have no energy but are inwardly getting stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' means pee: strip P, E and E from the outside of PEOPLE to leave OPL, then put A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone with shifting iridescent colours, a precious stone.

clue.text: Court action ruined kebab stall

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the food stall's name are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A lawsuit after a kebab stall was wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' sounds legal, but the court is a sports court.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketball is a game played on an indoor court, so it is action taking place on a court.

clue.text: A tube drunk in Oz is excellent

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: In Australia, getting drunk on the Tube counts as a great night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Oz' says the answer is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaut is Australian and New Zealand slang meaning outstanding or great.

clue.text: Timber manufacturer left a church without lead on roof

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the article and church go round the next letter
lead on means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: only the first letter of roof is wanted

explanation.surface: A builder left a church whose roof had no lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, and 'Timber manufacturer' is a tree that produces wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a conifer whose durable wood is used for building and fencing.

clue.text: Mary and Ted fixed the date to settle?

indicators.note: fixed means the names are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A couple named Mary and Ted set a wedding date to settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: A term day (quarter day) is when rents or debts fall due, the date to settle up.
explanation.definitionFit: A term day is one of the fixed days in the year when payments such as rent become due.

clue.text: I command military hospital unit accommodating fifty soldiers

indicators.note: accommodating means the ward takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a ward is a unit of a hospital
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A commander's boast about a military hospital ward housing fifty troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlord is a military leader who controls an area by force, someone who could say they command.

clue.text: Reporter's wise to squash point that's insubstantial

indicators.note: to squash means the two letters press the compass point between them
a reporter speaks, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word wise said aloud sounds like 'Ys', two letter Ys
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A journalist knows better than to quash a point that lacks substance.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'wise' is 'Ys', so two Ys sit either side of EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty can mean frothy, light and lacking substance, like foam on fermenting liquor.

clue.text: A case of passion suppressed by silence

indicators.note: suppressed by means the passion is held down inside the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
heat means intense passion

explanation.surface: A crime of passion hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover for a blade, so it is a kind of case.
